author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both the page and the reinstated JSON route
summary: Reinstate the machine-readable /vets route as a supported surface and let the veterinarian directory be narrowed to veterinarians holding a named specialty on both the browser page and that route. Whole-name, case-insensitive match; a blank name narrows nothing; no match yields an empty list at success; without the parameter both surfaces behave as today; filtered pages stay navigable.
acceptance_criteria: Without a specialty named, both the browser page and the machine-readable route return the full directory as they do today.
With a specialty naming a whole entry from the clinic's list, the browser page lists only veterinarians holding that specialty, a page at a time.
With the same named specialty, the machine-readable route returns only veterinarians holding that specialty.
A specialty differing from a stored one only by letter case matches; a name matching only the start of a specialty does not match.
A name matching no specialty succeeds with an empty veterinarian list rather than an error, on both surfaces.
A blank or whitespace-only specialty returns the full directory, as an empty owner search returns every owner, on both surfaces.
A filtered browser page with more results than fit one page keeps the specialty on later pages and shows only matching veterinarians.
The new behavior is covered by tests.
non_goals: A visible filter control — form, dropdown, or page control; the filter is URL-contract only this round and a control may follow
Free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope under the narrowed NG-9
notes: NG-9 narrowed via adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-narrow-vet-search-to-allow-specialty-filter.md; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and is not reused. Modeling decision under the narrowest reading of 'mint a fresh requirement ID': the JSON reinstatement and the filter are folded into one requirement (REQ-VET-003), the endpoint's first requested capability. Open question, non-blocking: if a future JSON-only capability arrives it takes its own REQ and REQ-VET-003 remains the directory's specialty filter. Behavioral note for design: the empty/whitespace-as-absent rule mirrors the existing empty owner-search behavior.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty filter mirrors the owner paged-search pattern onto the vet feature. OwnerController.processFindForm reads a param, strips/blank-checks it, and calls OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith with a Pageable (read at OwnerController.java:94-137, OwnerRepository.java:45); the vet side extends the same shape onto the two existing routes in VetController (showVetList findPaginated helper at VetController.java:44-72) backed by a declarative Spring Data query on VetRepository. No new pattern, module, or integration appears; this is the documented 'Spring Data derives implementations from method names' approach (system-design.md Overview, Contracts). Basis: direct reads of the cited files (IDE oracle not connected, so file reads are the resolution basis, stronger than grep).
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived query methods filtering by whole specialty name, case-insensitive: a Page overload (for /vets.html paging) and a Collection overload (for the /vets JSON route). Because Vet-Specialty is @ManyToMany (Vet.java:47), the join can yield duplicate Vet rows, so the derived query needs Distinct; case-insensitivity uses the IgnoreCase derived keyword.

VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each gain an optional specialty @RequestParam. Controller branches: blank/absent specialty routes to the existing findAll paths (behavior unchanged); a present specialty routes to the new filtered query. The JSON route builds its Vets wrapper from the filtered collection.

vetList.html pagination links (currently hard-coded /vets.html?page=N at lines 30-52) must carry the specialty parameter so filtered pages stay navigable; the controller must expose the (normalized) specialty as a model attribute for the template to append.

The /vets JSON route is reinstated as a supported surface under REQ-VET-003. Deferred to doc-sync post-implementation (kept code-authoritative, not written at triage): update system-design.md Known Defects row 3 ('machine-readable vet route serves no requirement / pending removal') and add REQ-VET-003 to the Implements columns for VetController, VetRepository, and Vets.

patterns.description: owner paged-search: param strip/blank-normalization plus PageRequest-backed repository call — the shape to mirror for the vet page route
existing findPaginated helper (pageSize=5, PageRequest.of(page-1,...)) that the filtered page query slots into

risks.risk: Blank-as-absent cannot reuse owner's empty-string trick: whole-name IgnoreCase equality against '' matches a specialty literally named '' (i.e. nothing), whereas findByLastNameStartingWith('') matches everything. Folding blank into the filter query would wrongly empty the directory.
risks.mitigation: Branch explicitly in the controller: blank/whitespace-only or absent specialty calls the existing findAll paths; only a non-blank specialty calls the filtered query.

risks.risk: @ManyToMany join between Vet and Specialty can return duplicate Vet rows for a matching specialty.
risks.mitigation: Use a Distinct derived query (e.g. findDistinctBySpecialties...).

risks.risk: Vendor case-insensitivity: relying on column collation reproduces the confirmed REQ-OWN-002 PostgreSQL case-sensitivity defect (system-design.md Known Defects).
risks.mitigation: Use the Spring Data IgnoreCase derived keyword, which generates UPPER(...) in JPQL and holds across all three vendors independent of collation.

risks.risk: VetRepository.findAll methods are @Cacheable("vets") with no eviction (Open Question #5); the new filtered methods interact with the same cache.
risks.mitigation: Non-blocking implementer choice: annotating the filtered methods @Cacheable("vets") is safe (cache keys differ by args, and there is no vet write path), or leave them uncached. Do not change the existing findAll cache behavior.

risks.risk: An implementer following system-design.md Known Defects row 3 might remove the /vets route as 'pending removal'.
risks.mitigation: REQ-VET-003 reinstates /vets as a supported surface; the route must be kept and extended, not deleted.

notes: ADR audit (triage-time coherence check, not the autofix audit): docs/adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-narrow-vet-search-to-allow-specialty-filter.md lands correctly in durable memory — filename carries the load-bearing 'non-goal-' infix (within product-requirements-expert write scope), its Implementation section uses '**Non-goal:** NG-9' per convention, it is indexed in docs/adr/README.md (2026-08-07, Accepted), and it is coherent with the 'Specialty filter' term in ubiquitous-language.md (Avoid: Search — whole-name filter over a displayed attribute, distinct from owner free-text prefix search). No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a silent skip. No system-design.md edits made at triage; the state corrections above are deferred to doc-sync to keep the doc code-authoritative until the filtering methods exist.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Specialty filter uses a Spring Data derived query (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) with parameter binding; no string-concatenated SQL, so the new query surface introduces no injection path.

Reflected-output encoding is sound: the user-supplied specialty reaches vetList.html only inside Thymeleaf link expressions @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encode the query-parameter value and HTML-attribute-escape the href. It is never rendered as raw HTML text, so no reflected XSS. The change also replaced the prior string-literal URL preprocessing with the safe parameterized link form.

Reinstated JSON /vets route exposes only the public vet directory (names and specialty names) already served by /vets.html; no new PII, credential, or authorization boundary is crossed, and Jackson serialization escapes output.

Input normalization is null-safe: normalizeSpecialty converts null to empty and strips whitespace before the isEmpty branch, so the blank-as-absent path cannot NPE or leak an unnormalized value into the query.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: @GetMapping({ "/vets" }) uses an unnecessary array literal for a single path. A reader scanning mappings sees braces and expects multiple paths; there is only one. The single-value form is the idiomatic Spring annotation style.

showResourcesVetList references the repository as this.vetRepository (lines 82, 85); findPaginated references it as vetRepository without the qualifier (lines 70, 72). The inconsistency within the same class forces a reader to verify that this.vetRepository and vetRepository are the same field rather than two different references.
findings.fix: Drop the this. prefix from lines 82 and 85 to match the style used in findPaginated and addPaginationModel.

findings.description: The local variable Collection<Vet> vets shadows the @Autowired VetRepository vets field at line 85. A reader tracing vets.isEmpty() must decide which vets is under inspection before verifying the assertion.
findings.fix: Rename the local variable to result or prefixResult.

findings.description: The controller adds specialty as an empty string to the model for the unfiltered case. Thymeleaf includes specialty= (empty value) in every pagination link when the directory is unfiltered, adding a spurious query parameter to all paging URLs. Behaviour is correct (the controller normalizes blank to absent) but the URLs carry unnecessary noise for unfiltered browsing.
findings.fix: Either pass null instead of empty string to the model attribute for the unfiltered case in VetController.showVetList (Thymeleaf omits null parameters), or adjust the template th:href expressions to suppress the parameter when specialty is empty: specialty=${specialty != '' ? specialty : null}.

approved_aspects: Format check passes with no violations (./gradlew checkFormat BUILD SUCCESSFUL)
Both new VetRepository methods correctly apply Distinct and IgnoreCase as required by the @ManyToMany join and the cross-collation case-insensitive requirement
Javadoc on the two new repository methods explains the Distinct and IgnoreCase derivation choices, giving a future reader enough context to verify correctness without re-deriving it
normalizeSpecialty centralizes null-safety and whitespace stripping into one private method, keeping both call sites symmetrical and readable
The blank-as-absent branch in findPaginated carries an inline comment explaining why blank cannot route to the filtered query, which is the non-obvious design constraint in this feature

Integration tests for case-insensitive match and prefix-nonmatch land in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest) — the correct layer for verifying Spring Data derived-query semantics against the real schema
All five pagination link variants in vetList.html carry the specialty parameter, satisfying the filtered-pagination navigability acceptance criterion

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: blankSpecialtyShouldReturnTheFullDirectory performs two independent acts (whitespace on the HTML surface, then blank on the JSON surface) in one test method. If the first perform assertion fails, the JSON surface is never exercised and its behavior is unknown. testing-principles.md requires four-phase linearity and one logical assertion per test. Split into blankSpecialtyShouldReturnTheFullDirectoryOnTheBrowserPage and blankSpecialtyShouldReturnTheFullDirectoryOnTheJsonRoute.
unmatchedSpecialtyShouldReturnEmptyListWithoutError performs two independent acts (HTML then JSON) in one method. Same isolation defect as above. Split into two tests, one per surface.

blankSpecialtyShouldReturnTheFullDirectory covers whitespace-only on the HTML surface and empty-string on the JSON surface, but not empty-string on HTML or whitespace-only on JSON. The PRD acceptance criterion (blank or whitespace-only, on either surface) implies all four input-by-surface combinations. After splitting per the finding above, each new test should cover both input variants (empty string and whitespace-only) for its surface.

No integration test covers findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable), the paginated overload used by the browser-page route. ClinicServiceTests tests the non-paginated overload for case-insensitivity and prefix exclusion, but the paginated method is a distinct Spring Data JPA query method that generates its own SQL. Add an integration test that calls the paginated overload and verifies: case-insensitive match returns the correct page of vets, and prefix does not match.

Three inline narration comments restate what the code already shows: the two surface labels in blankSpecialtyShouldReturnTheFullDirectory and the page-count arithmetic in filteredPaginationShouldCarryTheSpecialtyOnLaterPages. testing-principles.md prohibits prose that restates code. Remove the comments; rename the magic total-elements literal 12 to a named constant (e.g., TOTAL_MATCHING_VETS) so the reader can verify the setup without a comment.

approved_aspects: All new test method names follow the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school required by testing-principles.md
Controller tests use @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean for VetRepository, which is the sanctioned use of MockMvc as the HTTP-transport boundary mock
Integration tests use @DataJpaTest with real H2 database and no mocks for the repository layer, satisfying the real-I/O requirement
Private factory methods james(), helen(), henry() wrap new Vet() construction so test bodies never call production constructors directly
specialtyFilterShouldMatchWholeNameCaseInsensitively tests both lowercase and mixed-case inputs against seed data, confirming the IgnoreCase contract at the level where it is enforced
specialtyFilterShouldNotMatchOnPrefix uses a real prefix input against the real database, confirming whole-name semantics
filteredPaginationShouldCarryTheSpecialtyOnLaterPages verifies the model attribute and the rendered pagination link both carry the specialty parameter
All seven PRD acceptance criteria for REQ-VET-003 are exercised at least partially across the two test files

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Round-2 delta introduces no security regression. The specialty request param reaches VetRepository only through the Spring Data derived query findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, which generates a parameterized query — no SQL/JPQL injection surface, unchanged from round 1.

Reflected-output picture cleared in round 1 holds: specialty is reflected only inside Thymeleaf @{/vets.html(page=..,specialty=${specialty})} URL expressions, which URL-encode query-parameter values — no reflected XSS or URL/parameter injection.

The null-vs-empty-string model attribute change is security-neutral-to-positive: null makes Thymeleaf's link builder omit the parameter entirely rather than emit specialty=, narrowing the reflected surface. It does not route specialty into any new sink.
normalizeSpecialty null-guards and strips input before both the query and the model; no unvalidated data crosses a new boundary. No supply-chain change in this delta.
